a1
Famine reached Canaan. Jacob sent ten sons to Egypt for grain, but kept Benjamin home.
a2
The brothers bowed before Joseph. He knew them, but they did not know him.
b1
Joseph said: you are spies. They said: we are twelve brothers; the youngest is home, and one is no more.
b2
After three days he said: I fear God. Let one stay here, and bring your youngest brother.
c1
They said to one another: this is punishment for what we did to Joseph. We saw his anguish, and would not listen.
c2
Joseph understood them. He turned away and wept. Then he had Simeon bound before their eyes.
d1
He had their silver put back in their sacks. When they found it, their hearts sank: what has God done to us?
d2
At home, Jacob said: Joseph is gone, Simeon is gone, and now you would take Benjamin. He will not go.
h1
Years later, the brothers finally spoke of what they had done to Joseph.
h2
The wrong had not stayed buried. It had only been waiting.
h3
Facing a wrong is where repair can begin.
h4
Today, name one wrong you have been avoiding, and bring it to God.
i
What old wrong are you ready to face?
